sections.html:
Montana's most populous county, Yellowstone, has Billings as its seat and biggest city and counted 164,731 residents in 2020. The Yellowstone River runs through it from southwest to northeast. Billings, Laurel and Broadview are the incorporated places, and the rest of the county is unincorporated, including communities such as Huntley, Lockwood, Shepherd and Worden.

It helps to think of the county as several markets. A Billings neighborhood house, a farm parcel near Shepherd and a lot in Broadview all go through the same county offices, but they sit in different school and utility districts. A home inside a city carries city levies on top of county and school levies. A home in Lockwood or Huntley is billed with its own school and special districts. Rural parcels often add well, septic and road access questions that a city lot never raises.

Many districts means two houses of equal value can get different tax bills, and buyers often compare the bills before anything else.

The Yellowstone County Treasurer collects the tax. The Montana Department of Revenue sets the values. The Treasurer's office also issues tax deeds and tax lien assignment certificates, records miscellaneous revenue and handles tax protests and mobile home moving permits.

  • Treasurer: Room 113, 2825 3rd Ave N, Billings, MT 59101
  • Mailing address: P.O. Box 35010, Billings, MT 59107
  • Phone: 406-256-2802
  • Tax Appeal Board: 406-256-2701, P.O. Box 35001, Billings

You can search your parcel on the county's tax records search or read the property tax page. The office collects about $345 million a year in real and personal property taxes and handles roughly 75,000 real estate bills, 5,900 mobile home bills and 1,050 personal property bills, so due dates and penalties are applied strictly.

Real estate tax is paid in two halves by 5 PM Mountain Time. If a date falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies.

Yellowstone County payment due dates
Tax typeFirst halfSecond half
Real estateNovember 30 (2026 only: December 3)May 31 (2027 only: June 1)
Mobile homeMay 31 (2027 only: June 1)November 30
Personal propertyJune 30None

Late taxes carry a 2% penalty plus interest of 5/6 of 1% each month. That covers real property, personal property, mobile homes and farm and ranch property. This year's first-half date moved to December 3, so if you are closing in late November or early December, ask your title company which date it is using.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes go delinquent
sections.html:
The county attaches a tax lien, and a third party may then buy an assignment of it. Assignments are sold in late August, with a $50 fee for each one.

The steps after that are slow and involve several notices. Lienholders may pay later delinquent taxes on an assigned parcel only between June 1 and July 30 (June 2 to July 30 in 2027). In the last year of the redemption period, a notice that a tax deed may be issued goes out between May 1 and May 30. A tax deed carries a $25 deed fee plus recording fees of $20 for the first page and $10 for each added page.

The county does not give legal advice to people who buy tax liens. If a lien on your house has been assigned, treat it as a payoff item. The title company has to clear it, including the lienholder's interest and costs. The county's tax lien page has the certificate list and the current rules, which changed after recent legislation.

Object in writing within 30 days of the date on the classification and appraisal notice. Doing so keeps your appeal alive for both years of the two-year valuation cycle on residential and commercial property. Timing follows Montana Code Annotated sections 15-7-102 and 15-15-102:

  • You may submit one application for reduction per valuation cycle.
  • An objection filed after 30 days applies only to the second year, and must be in by June 1 of that year.
  • The 30 days run from the date on the notice, not the date you received it, and no extra mailing days are added.
  • Only the County Tax Appeal Board can decide whether a late appeal had good cause, such as a notice mailed to the wrong address.

After an informal Department of Revenue review, you can appeal that result to the county board, and then to the State Tax Appeal Board. Boards can look at an actual selling price, independent appraisals and other evidence of market value. Send completed forms to the Clerk and Recorder's office.

Unpaid tax is settled from the seller's proceeds at closing. The title company asks the Treasurer for the balance, including any penalty and monthly interest, and pays it out of the sale.

The steps look like this:

  • Ask the Treasurer for the current amount owed on your parcel.
  • If a lien has been assigned to an investor, get a written payoff from the lienholder too, since its costs are added.
  • Hand both figures to the title company before you accept a price.
  • Pay by the due date if you can, because the 5/6 of 1% monthly interest keeps growing.

A cash buyer can close around a tax balance, since the payoff comes from the sale. We buy houses as-is and do not promise a price before we see the property.

Mobile homes and personal property run on their own calendar, as the table above shows: personal property is due June 30, and a mobile home's first half comes due May 31. A seller with a mobile home should confirm both halves are paid before closing, and the Treasurer's office can tell you the balance. The same office issues mobile home moving permits, so ask about one if the home will leave the lot.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Yellowstone County?
faqs.a: The Yellowstone County Treasurer collects it, and the Montana Department of Revenue sets the values. The office is at 2825 3rd Ave N, Room 113 in Billings, and the phone number is 406-256-2802.

faqs.q: When is real estate tax due in Yellowstone County?
faqs.a: November 30 and May 31 by 5 PM Mountain Time, with the next business day applying on weekends and holidays. For 2026 the first half is due December 3, and for 2027 the second half is due June 1.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Yellowstone County?
faqs.a: Late taxes carry a 2% penalty plus interest of 5/6 of 1% per month. That applies to real property, personal property, mobile homes and farm and ranch property.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my valuation?
faqs.a: You have 30 days from the date on the appraisal notice for the appeal to cover the full two-year cycle. A later appeal applies only to the second year and must be filed by June 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Yellowstone County house if there is a tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien and any related costs are paid from your proceeds at closing, so get a written payoff from the Treasurer and any lienholder before closing.
